from collections import deque

def simulate_game(n, m, frogs):
    board = [False] * m  # A set to mark cells with frogs on them
    frog_queue = deque()
    frog_queue.extend(frogs)
    ai = [f[1] for f in frogs]  # Initial jump lengths
    
    while frog_queue:
        frog = frog_queue.pop()
        original_frog_pos = frog[0] - 1  # Adjusting positions so that each frog starts at 0
        target_pos = (original_frog_pos + ai[f[1]] - 1) % m  # Determine the final position, adjusting for cyclic nature

            ai[f[1]] = max(ai[f[1]] - frog[1], 0)  # Update jump length if the frog was already on the board

            board[target_pos] = True  # Mark the cell as occupied by this frog
            frog_queue.appendleft(frog)  # Add frog to the queue for the next turn
    
    surviver = [index for index, status in enumerate(board) if not status]
    return len(surviver), surviver

# Example input

def min_cost_to_connect_rectangles(N, rectangles):
    l_sorted = sorted([i for i, j in rectangles], reverse=True)
    r_sorted = sorted([j + 1 for i, j in rectangles])
    
    min_cost = float('inf')
    for i in range(1, int(math.sqrt(N)) + 1):

        mi = min(r_sorted[0], l_sorted[0] + i)
